ideas.title: Tick of the Gun
ideas.short_description: A post-apocalyptic western puzzle roguelike: every gunman shoots when you do. Arrange the chaos so you are the last one standing.
ideas.description: Two hundred years after the bombs, the West is wild again, and every meeting ends with guns drawn. Each encounter in this roguelike puzzle game is a frozen standoff on a small isometric grid: raiders, scavengers and rogue robots, each aiming at someone, each with a rule for how they react. Every action you take, a step, a shot, a dive behind a wreck or a kicked fuel barrel, moves the world forward one tick, and every bullet in the air moves with it. Read the lines of fire, predict who will shoot whom, and turn the standoff into a readable bullet hell that ends with you still breathing. Each standoff is a logic puzzle with a clean solution, but the wasteland is procedurally generated and death is permanent. Between encounters, recruit drifters with strange guns and stranger rules, patch up your ride and push further down the highway. Short runs, arcade-quick retries and brutally difficult late fights. Count every bullet and walk away.
ideas.pitch: A permadeath wasteland roguelike where every fight is a frozen multi-gunman standoff and bullets advance one tick per action, so a bullet hell becomes a readable logic puzzle you solve to be the last one standing.
ideas.interpretation: The decoded tags (strategy, puzzle, action, roguelike, difficult, shooter, bullet hell, turn-based, post-apocalyptic, logic) and parents (One Shot All Kill, Everyone Must Die, Viking Nudgers, 2080 APOCALYPSE) point to turn-based shooting puzzles in a ruined world. Turret-crossfire, falling-wreckage and time-stops bullet-hell takes scored lower than tick-based post-apocalyptic standoffs. The final game deliberately differs from the Everyone Must Die neighbour: here you survive rather than make everyone die, and it adds a roguelike road trip, drifter recruits and visible bullet travel.

nearest.name: Everyone Must Die: A Western Standoff

ideas.title: Loaded Die
ideas.short_description: You are a die. Every time you tumble, the face that lands on top changes how you jump, dash and fight. Roll through brutal pixel-art platforming runs, solo or in couch co-op, where the right number at the right moment is everything.
ideas.description:
Somewhere in a forgotten arcade cabinet, a single six-sided die has escaped the board. Now it has to roll, bounce and flip its way through a crumbling world of tiles and traps to get home.

You do not just move, you tumble. Each roll turns the die a quarter turn, and the face that lands on top decides your power: one lets you float, two gives a double jump, three a wall cling, four a ground pound, five a dash, and six a burst of fire. Every screen is a small puzzle: count your rolls so the right face is up before you reach the gap, the spikes or the enemy.

Runs are built from random side-scrolling rooms with bouncy, physics-driven movement, crumbling platforms, conveyor belts, card-soldier enemies and loaded dice that cheat. Between floors you carve new pips onto your faces, swap abilities and gamble on risky upgrades that reshape your whole build.

It is a difficult, arcade-fast platformer with a roguelite heart, plus a casual mode with extra checkpoints. Bring a friend in local co-op as a second die and roll together.
ideas.pitch: A precision platformer where how you move is itself the puzzle: whichever face of the die lands on top sets your current ability, so you plan every roll ahead, and a roguelite layer lets you rewrite the faces between floors.
ideas.interpretation: The void is a tight 2D pixel-art action platformer with strong Puzzle, Roguelite and Physics signals and some couch co-op. Its parents (Blockdown's grid rolling, Tilebound's tile-built loadouts, HEXED DELTA's geometric shapes, Wood Guy's physics) point to a rolling-block hero whose orientation is the build. The nearest existing game, DICEASTER, uses faces as health. This game uses them as abilities.

controls.title: Secondhand Truth
controls.short_description: Plant one whispered sentence in a medieval market town and watch it change as it passes from mouth to mouth. Steer the gossip through boasters, mishearers and zealots so the right version reaches the right ear by nightfall.
controls.description: A small medieval market town runs on routine: the baker opens at dawn, the washerwomen meet at the river, the guards drink at the tavern after the evening bell. You are a stranger with one tool, a whispered sentence. Each chapter sets a goal, such as freeing a wrongly jailed tanner or stopping a forced marriage, and a version of the truth that must reach a particular ear before nightfall. Choose who hears your words first, then watch the day unfold in pausable real time as the sentence travels. Every listener retells it in their own way. The boaster doubles every number, the half-deaf blacksmith swaps similar-sounding words, the priest adds a moral, and the skeptic strips out the juicy part. Changes stack, so a harmless remark about a missing goat can reach the magistrate as an accusation of witchcraft. Study schedules and temperaments, intercept the story with a second whisper to correct its course, and never speak to the same person twice, or suspicion will trace the tale back to you. Each chapter has several solutions, and the outcomes carry into the next.
controls.pitch: The unit you control is gossip itself: a sentence that mutates predictably through each townsperson's personality, turning a social network into a routing puzzle.

controls.title: The Lip Reader
controls.short_description: From a rented attic above a divided city, spy on conversations you can never hear. Decode lip movements frame by frame, rebuild what was said, and decide whose secrets end up in your report.
controls.description: It is the winter of a long cold war, and your agency has given you a telephoto camera, a pair of binoculars and an attic window above a busy square full of cafes, tram stops and embassy doors. You cannot hear a single word below, but you can read lips. Each case begins with surveillance: track targets, catch them mid-conversation, and record short reels of film. Back at your desk you scrub through the footage frame by frame and match mouth shapes to sounds. Many sounds look identical on the lips, so 'bomb', 'mop' and 'pop' share a shape, and only context, gestures and what you already know can tell them apart. Assemble the fragments into a transcript, flag the uncertain words, and file your report. Your superiors act on what you write, so a single misread can burn an innocent courier or let a defector slip away. As the cases connect, you start to notice that someone in the square is choosing their words very carefully, as if they know exactly where you are watching from.
controls.pitch: Lip-reading becomes the core deduction mechanic, where visually identical mouth shapes create real ambiguity that the player resolves through context and evidence.

controls.title: The Quiet Meter
controls.short_description: Solve crimes in a twelve-storey apartment block using nothing but minute-by-minute electricity, water and gas readings. Learn every appliance's signature, rebuild each resident's night, and find the reading that should not exist.
controls.description: A building is a diary that nobody meant to write. As a forensic analyst for the city's utility company, you are called in when the police have run out of witnesses. Each case hands you a block of flats and a night's worth of meter data: electricity, water and gas, sampled every minute for every unit. At first it is just lines on a chart. Then you learn to read them. A sharp three-minute spike is a kettle. Hot water paired with a gas burner is a shower. A slow rhythmic wave is a washing machine on its spin cycle. Tag these signatures, place them on a shared timeline, and the residents come alive: who woke at three, who pretended to be away, which empty flat suddenly drew power for exactly forty minutes. Cross-reference units to catch people moving between them, test theories against the data, and submit a reconstruction that must account for every anomaly. Later buildings add solar panels, faulty wiring, shared boilers and suspects who know how to disguise their footprint.
controls.pitch: Detective work done entirely from household utility consumption curves, turning appliance signatures into the evidence and the timeline into the solution.

controls.title: The Interpreter's Chair
controls.short_description: Two nations are negotiating a ceasefire, and you are the only person in the room who understands both sides. Translate faithfully, or quietly bend every sentence toward the peace you believe in, without getting caught.
controls.description: A ceasefire summit has been arranged in a remote mountain hotel, and you are the sole interpreter between two delegations who share no common language. Every word passes through you. As each speaker talks, you hear the full meaning, including the threat hidden in a polite phrase and the concession a general did not mean to offer. Then you choose how to deliver it. Render it faithfully, soften an insult, sharpen a vague promise, drop a dangerous aside, or slip in a phrase of your own. The table reacts in real time: tempers rise and cool, trust grows or collapses, and positions on the map shift. Your manipulation is not invisible. Each side has aides who understand fragments of the other language, and a careless change can be noticed, recorded and used against you. Between sessions, corridors, dinners and late phone calls let both sides press you for private favours. Five days of talks lead to many endings, from lasting peace to renewed war to your own quiet disappearance.
controls.pitch: The player is the communication channel itself, editing every sentence of a negotiation while partially bilingual witnesses threaten to expose the edits.

nearest.name: Prolegomena To a Hyperdimensional Interface That Will Be Able to Manifest From Three-Minute Interchanges

controls.title: Sold to the Back Row
controls.short_description: Become a fast-talking auctioneer. Keep your bid chant locked to the beat while scanning a packed room for nods, winks and twitching paddles, and squeeze every last coin from the crowd before the hammer falls.
controls.description: Auctioneering is music with money attached, and you are about to learn the rhythm. Each lot opens with a starting price and a room full of bidders. Your chant is a rhythm track: hit the beats to keep the filler words rolling and the crowd hypnotised, and if you stumble the room loses interest. While your mouth runs, your eyes work. Bidders signal in tiny ways: a raised catalogue, a tap of the nose, a glance to a partner, a paddle lifted half an inch. Spot a bid, point at it on the beat, and the price climbs a step. Every bidder has a hidden budget and a temperament, so read their hesitation, coax them with a smaller increment, or bluff a bid from the back wall if you dare. Drop the hammer too early and you leave money on the table; wait too long and the lot goes unsold. Work your way from livestock barns and storage lockers to estate sales and glittering city galleries, then face rival auctioneers in a split-screen chant-off.
controls.pitch: A rhythm game fused with crowd-reading, where keeping the auction chant on beat and spotting subtle bids must happen at the same time.

controls.title: Card Section
controls.short_description: Plan the giant pictures that thousands of fans make by holding up coloured cards, then conduct them live on match day. Late arrivals, swapped seats and distracted children will ruin your masterpiece unless you react fast.
controls.description: Halftime is in ninety seconds and twelve thousand people are about to become your pixels. In the planning phase you design card stunts for a stadium's seating: draw a mosaic on the seat grid, break it into frames for animated sequences, and print an instruction slip for every seat. You choose how complicated each slip should be, because a clever ten-step animation means nothing if fans cannot follow it. On match day the plan meets the public. Spectators arrive late, sit in the wrong row, drop their cards, hold them upside down, or wander off for snacks just before the big reveal. You conduct from the press box in real time: call each flip over the loudspeaker, spot gaps forming in your image, send volunteers running with spare cards, and improvise simpler fallbacks when a section falls apart. Images are scored for accuracy and crowd excitement, unlocking larger venues and trickier stands. Friends can join online, each conducting their own block of seats, and a design editor lets you share stunts with the community.
controls.pitch: An entire stadium crowd becomes an unreliable pixel display that you design for in advance and then conduct live as people fail to follow instructions.

controls.title: Rounds and Changes
controls.short_description: Ring tower bells the old way with friends: each player pulls one heavy swinging bell, swapping places in shifting mathematical patterns while keeping every stroke perfectly in time.
controls.description: High in a village church tower, eight ropes hang in a circle. Each one is attached to a bell weighing as much as a small car, and each is yours to control. This kind of ringing is not about melodies. The bells sound one after another in rows, and with every row the order changes according to a pattern called a method. Your job is to know where your bell belongs in each row and get it there. Pull harder to hold the bell up longer and strike later; check your pull to come in sooner. Overdo it and the bell swings past its balance point and the whole band falls apart. Ring alone with patient computer ringers, or join up to seven friends online, each on a rope, while one of you conducts, calling out changes that rearrange the pattern mid-flow. The campaign follows a neglected tower brought back to life: recruit locals, learn new methods, ring for weddings and festivals, and train for a marathon touch of thousands of unbroken changes.
controls.pitch: A co-op rhythm game built on the real tradition of change ringing, where the challenge is timing a heavy swinging bell while tracking your place in a moving permutation.

controls.title: Unseen Stage
controls.short_description: A street mime whose imaginary walls, ladders and ropes become solid, but only while someone is watching. Gather an audience, hold their attention, and perform your way across a city that has forgotten how to pretend.
controls.description: In a grey city where nobody has time for street performers, a silent mime discovers that a convincing act becomes real. Trace a wall with your palms and it blocks the way. Climb an imaginary rope hand over hand and you rise. Lean on a counter that is not there and it holds your weight. There is one condition: the object exists only while an audience member is watching and believing. Every level is a puzzle about attention. Gather onlookers, keep them entertained, and lead them to places where their gaze covers the gaps you need to cross. Children believe almost anything, office workers glance away to check the time, and a stern critic needs a flawless performance before your ladder turns solid. Lose the crowd mid-climb and you fall. Perform gestures with precise inputs, chain them into routines, and use your invisible creations to trap guards, lift friends and cross rooftops. The wordless story, told in hand-drawn panels, follows the mime as the city slowly learns to play again.
controls.pitch: Pantomimed objects are solid only inside an audience's line of sight, so crowd attention becomes the platforming resource the player must earn and steer.

controls.title: Root Exchange
controls.short_description: Become the fungus beneath an old forest and run its hidden marketplace. Thread through the soil, link tree roots, broker sugar for minerals, and take your cut while keeping the whole forest alive through drought and rivals.
controls.description: Beneath every old forest lies a network of fungal threads linking the roots of trees, and you are that network. Trees make sugar in the sunlight but struggle to pull minerals and water from the soil; you mine minerals but cannot make sugar. Every connection you grow is a trading route. Extend threads through layers of earth, wrap the roots of oaks, pines and birches, and set exchange rates with each tree. Ferry surplus sugar from sunlit giants to shaded saplings, move water toward the thirsty in a dry spell, and skim a share from every transaction to fund further growth. The forest responds to your choices. Starve the young trees and the canopy thins within a decade; overcharge the old ones and they cut you off and court a rival fungus spreading from the next valley. Seasons shift demand, beetles and drought test your reserves, and loggers can sever whole districts overnight. When your network is strong, raise mushrooms above ground to send spores toward new forests with harsher conditions.
controls.pitch: The player is the underground fungal network that brokers nutrients between trees, an ecological trading economy seen entirely from the soil.

controls.title: Long Water
controls.short_description: You are a river flowing across ten thousand years. Carve valleys, choose where silt settles, flood and retreat, and shape the towns that rise on your banks while they build dams and walls to bend you to their will.
controls.description: Begin as meltwater at the edge of a retreating glacier and end, if you endure, as a broad delta spilling into the sea. Each turn spans a decade. Spend the strength of your current to cut into an outer bank, drop silt on an inner bend, abandon a loop to leave an oxbow lake, or gather spring rain into a flood that spreads fertile mud across the plain. Life answers your choices. Reeds, fish and herons follow clean shallows, and people follow the fish. Villages appear where your soil is richest, and they love you while you feed them. As they grow, they begin to argue with you: mills narrow your channel, embankments pin you in place, bridges ask you to stay still, and eventually a dam threatens to stop you altogether. You can bend around them, nourish them, or break them with a hundred-year flood. Every valley is procedurally shaped, and every playthrough leaves a different map of towns, wetlands and ruins along the path you chose.
controls.pitch: The player is a river across millennia, shaping its own course while the civilizations it feeds work to pin it in place.

controls.title: Fair or Foul
controls.short_description: Become the weather watcher of a stormy nineteenth-century fishing village. Read clouds, pressure and seabirds each dawn, raise your forecast on the harbour mast, and live with what happens when the boats come home, or don't.
controls.description: The fishing boats will not leave the harbour until they see your flag. As the new weather watcher of a small village on a wild northern coast in the nineteenth century, your forecast decides whether families eat this week and whether some of them come back at all. Each dawn you climb to the station and observe. The sky is fully simulated, with fronts, pressure systems and cloud formations that behave as they do in reality, so a thickening veil of high cloud, a falling barometer and a wind backing to the south all mean something. Combine your instruments with the village's own signs: gulls staying ashore, an old sailor's aching knee, a halo around the moon. Then raise a fair, caution or storm signal on the harbour mast and watch the fleet decide. Your accuracy builds trust, and trust changes behaviour, since a doubted forecaster is ignored on the day it matters most. Over the seasons, upgrade instruments, keep a logbook of patterns, trade readings with distant stations by telegraph, and get to know the people whose lives ride on your judgement.
controls.pitch: A forecasting game where the player reads a physically simulated sky to make daily predictions whose credibility decides a village's fortunes.

controls.title: Valley Fold
controls.short_description: Fold your own army. Every crease you make on a square of paper decides how your units move, strike and survive, then they march into turn-based battles across a cluttered scholar's desk.
controls.description: On a scholar's desk at night, paper armies wage war across open books, ink pools and the ridges of a fallen ruler. You do not recruit soldiers; you fold them. Each unit starts as a blank square on a crease grid. Place mountain and valley folds, collapse the sheet, and the shape you create becomes the unit. Long sharp points give reach, extra flaps become legs and speed, stacked layers turn into armour, and broad wings let a piece glide from the rim of a teacup. Simple folds are reliable; ambitious ones are powerful but tricky to collapse correctly. Then take the fight to the grid in turn-based battles where terrain matters: ink soaks and weakens paper, a desk fan scatters light units, and a candle is as deadly as it sounds. Damaged units come back creased and torn, and you can refold them between fights, but every refold weakens the sheet. Collect new papers, from thin tissue to stiff card and metal foil, as you push through a roguelite campaign across a sprawling study.
controls.pitch: Unit design is literal paper folding: the geometry of the crease pattern you fold becomes the unit's stats in tactical combat.

nearest.name: Deep Tactics - Journey of the Wizard

controls.title: The Last Tuning
controls.short_description: A piano tuner is hired to restore every instrument in a shuttered mansion. Tune by ear, string by string, as each sour note you correct quiets something in the house, and each one you leave wavering draws it closer.
controls.description: In the autumn of 1926 you are hired to tune every piano in a shuttered country house: the grand in the ballroom, the upright in the servants' hall, the toy piano in the nursery and dozens more. The family will not say why, and they will not stay the night. Tuning works the way it does in real life. Open the instrument, set your lever on a pin, and listen. Two strings slightly apart produce a wavering beat; turn the pin until the beat slows and vanishes, or until it pulses at the exact rate a tempered interval needs. Play with headphones and the house becomes an instrument too. Every piano you set right calms part of the presence that lives here and reveals a fragment of the composer who once did. Every wavering, sour note attracts it. You cannot fight it and you cannot run far, so you must decide how much noise to make, which rooms to finish first, and when to stop and simply listen. Letters, scores and old recordings slowly reveal what was left unfinished.
controls.pitch: A horror game whose central skill is authentic by-ear piano tuning, with acoustic beating serving as both the puzzle and the thing that summons danger.

controls.title: Morning Control
controls.short_description: Lead the avalanche crew at a mountain resort. Dig snow pits before dawn, read the buried layers, choose which slopes to blast or close, and open the mountain safely before the first chairlift turns.
controls.description: Every morning the mountain asks a question, and you have until the lifts open to answer it. As head of the avalanche team at a busy ski resort, you start in darkness with overnight reports: snowfall, wind direction and temperature swings that may have buried a weak layer under a fresh slab. Choose which slopes to investigate, ski out with your crew, and dig. Each snow pit is a cross-section of the season, and reading it is a puzzle of crystal shapes, hardness and test results that tell you whether a slope will hold. Then decide: throw hand charges, fire the avalanche cannon, ski-cut a slope yourself, or keep it roped off for the day. The resort manager wants the famous runs open by nine, the guests want fresh powder, and the mountain does not care about either. Through the day, sun and wind keep changing the picture, so you reopen, close and respond to rescues. Seasons build on one another, since every storm and every decision is buried in the snowpack you will dig through next month.
controls.pitch: Snow science as the core loop: reading a layered snowpack and triggering controlled slides, with the whole season's weather persisting as buried history.

controls.title: Altitude Only
controls.short_description: A long-distance balloon race where your only control is up or down. Read invisible rivers of wind stacked in the sky, spend your ballast wisely, and drift hundreds of miles to the target ahead of your rivals.
controls.description: Gas balloons have no engine, no rudder and no steering wheel. You can rise by dropping sand and sink by venting gas, and that is all. Yet the sky is layered, with each altitude carrying its own wind, and a good pilot steers by choosing which layer to ride. Before each race, study forecasts and launch small pilot balloons to see how winds turn with height. In the air, watch cloud drift, chimney smoke and other racers for clues, then commit: climb into a fast westerly, drop into a slow southerly to curve around a mountain range, or hold steady and wait for the evening shift. Every climb costs ballast and every descent costs gas, and both run out. Races cover hundreds of miles and play out over hours compressed into tense, quiet sessions, ending in a precise landing near a target. Online, everyone shares the same simulated sky, so watching another balloon swing away reveals a wind you cannot see, while simply copying a rival means you can never beat them.
controls.pitch: A racing game with a single vertical control, where steering means reading and choosing between invisible stacked layers of wind.

controls.title: The Night Compositor
controls.short_description: Work the night shift at a nineteenth-century newspaper, setting every word by hand in backwards metal type. Justify lines, fit columns around adverts, and lock the front page before the presses roll at dawn.
controls.description: It is midnight in a city newsroom in the 1890s, and tomorrow's paper does not exist yet. Stories arrive in scrawled handwriting, and you must turn them into metal. Pick letters from the type case, where every letter has its own compartment, and drop them into your composing stick, upside down and mirrored. Fill each line exactly, using thin and wide spaces to justify it, because a loose line will fall out on the press. Then lay the finished columns into the page frame, a fitting puzzle of headlines, advertisements and illustrations that must lock together without gaps. The clock never stops. Breaking news forces you to tear up a finished column, the editor wants a bigger headline, the censor sends a list of words to cut, and the type case runs short of capital letters halfway through an election story, so you have to rephrase on the fly. Each morning the printed paper shows your mistakes in public. Between shifts, hire apprentices, buy new typefaces, and follow the stories that slowly reveal what is happening in the city.
controls.pitch: Hand-setting mirrored metal type under a deadline, combining typing, word-fitting and spatial page layout into a single job loop.

calibration.title: Final Bell Lockdown
calibration.short_description: On the final day of term, six classmates wake up sealed inside their academy with the air slowly running out, and the only way out is to kill someone and fool the others. A free murder-mystery visual novel.
calibration.description: The final afternoon of the school year should have been a celebration. Instead, six teenagers find every door and window of their academy locked tight, and a voice over the intercom explains the rules: the building's oxygen will be cut off once the clock runs down in half a day. There is a single exception. Whoever takes the life of a classmate, and then avoids being exposed as the culprit, gets to walk free. You follow the story as the hours slip away, talking with the other students, searching classrooms and hallways for clues, and watching trust between old friends crumble. When a body turns up, the investigation begins: gather evidence, question alibis, and work out who did it and how before the killer escapes. Accuse the wrong person and everyone pays. Told through anime-style art, with flashes of dark humor between the brutal moments, this free visual novel is a tense whodunit about pressure, guilt and what ordinary kids will do when survival depends on betrayal.

nearest.name: There’s No Way the Dating Sim Heroine I Liked Could Be a Murderer...?!

calibration.title: Shardlight Vigil
calibration.short_description: Shield a glowing crystal holding your trapped companion from a world swallowed by shadow. Push back the gloom, harvest its power, and place defenders before the creatures it births grow too strong in this roguelite defense game.
calibration.description: A thick, living blackness blankets every map you enter, and anything that brushes against it wakes a monster hungry for the one thing you care about: a crystal with your closest friend sealed inside. Each attempt begins with that crystal and a small reserve of energy. From there, the choices are yours. Peel back the shadow tile by tile, drain the power locked within it, and station guardians to cut down whatever crawls out. Or gamble on bold expeditions into the unknown to reach forgotten ruins and relics that can swing a run in your favor. The clock never stops: foes toughen with every passing second, so you must keep growing faster than they do by spending resources, stacking boosts and improving your units. Maps are generated fresh each time, bringing new layouts, threats and surprises. When a run ends, the minerals you salvaged feed a persistent upgrade tree that opens new defenders, abilities and starting perks. Mix those upgrades to discover combos that let you hold out longer, and keep returning until the gloom finally breaks.

calibration.title: Shapeshift Summer: The Crystal Curse
calibration.short_description: A sinister sorcerer has unleashed crystal-born monsters across Europe during a family road trip. Swap between alien forms to fight, solve puzzles and uncover secrets in a colorful 3D world, alone or with a friend on the couch.
calibration.description: A summer holiday across Europe was supposed to be a break for a ten-year-old hero and his relatives. Then a scheming spellcaster stirs four ancient crystals to life, ripping open a rift that pours otherworldly creatures into quiet villages and busy cities. You take control of the boy and his wrist-mounted device, which lets him morph into a roster of extraterrestrial forms, each with its own strengths: a crystal-bodied fighter that fires shards, a hulking four-armed brawler that smashes obstacles, and a blazing form that hurls flames. Switch forms on the fly to beat back monsters, clear environmental puzzles and reach hidden areas. Between fights, roam freely through towns, woodlands and alpine peaks, lend a hand to locals with side tasks, and pick up collectibles and power boosts that strengthen your transformations. His cousin and grandfather offer support and plenty of banter along the way. A second player can join on the same screen as a tough rival-turned-ally for split-screen cooperation. Track down the source of the crystals and confront the sorcerer in a climactic final battle.

calibration.title: Nubbin and the Captive Spirits
calibration.short_description: Hop, punch and leap through six vibrant pixel-art worlds as a tiny armless, legless heroine and her spirit buddy, freeing captured spirits and toppling the tyrant who has seized their island home.
calibration.description: Cast in the mold of the side-scrollers many of us grew up on, this hand-built pixel adventure stars a cheerful heroine with no arms or legs and her floating spirit companion. A cruel tyrant has seized their island, locking away its guardian spirits and ruling with an iron fist. Your job is to cross six distinct regions, each packed with hazards, enemies and hidden corners, and put an end to his rule. Moment to moment you run, leap and throw punches, timing every jump carefully because the stages reward exact movement and punish carelessness. Scattered throughout are strange chaotic energies the pair can tap into, opening new ways to cross gaps, reach high ledges and crack platforming puzzles. Each world ends with a demanding boss fight that tests what you have learned, and rescuing the imprisoned spirits along the way is part of the road to the final showdown. Bright colors, bouncy animation and tight controls give it a classic feel, and every sprite, level and tune was crafted by a person rather than generated by a machine.

calibration.title: Whisker Siege VR
calibration.short_description: Room-scale VR tower defense where adorable kittens are really hostile invaders from space. Build and upgrade weapons across floating island battlefields to stop the furry horde and take back your world.
calibration.description: The cuddly cats overrunning your homeworld are not pets at all. They are hostile extraterrestrials wearing fluffy disguises, and they have already seized almost everything. In this tower defense game designed from the ground up for room-scale virtual reality, you stand over a chain of fifteen floating islands, each with its own look and layout, and fight to keep the felines from reaching the key points that hold your territory. Lean in, look around the battlefield and place turrets and traps by hand along the routes the invaders travel. As waves grow larger they do not march in neat lines but spill across the terrain, and later attackers strap on protective gear built to shrug off certain kinds of fire. Respond by improving your arsenal, with more than fifty upgrades to unlock, and by pairing damage types against specific armor. A story campaign ramps the challenge from gentle to brutal, while a skirmish mode lets you replay any island on your own terms. It is strategic, a little absurd, and surprisingly tense.

calibration.title: Support Class Blues
calibration.short_description: Play the party member nobody thanks, the healer, keeping a squad of incompetent, ungrateful adventurers alive in real-time fights. Juggle your mana and endure their tantrums in this fantasy comedy RPG.
calibration.description: Every fantasy band of heroes has one person quietly holding it together, and in this lighthearted RPG that person is you. You sign on as the healer for a squad of glory-hungry misfits: a domineering shield-bearer, a vain bowman, a mage with questionable morals, and a berserker who never stops shouting. Fights unfold in real time, and you are the one watching the health bars. Restore wounds before they become fatal, cleanse poisons, curses and other nasty ailments, and hand out buffs, all while rationing a mana pool that drains far too quickly. Let a companion fall and they will remember it, sulking and underperforming in later battles until you smooth things over with potions, protective magic or a well-chosen line of dialogue. Twenty-two spells, branching skill trees and upgrades let you shape a personal style of support, and you can win rare gear to equip your teammates. Conversations let you lean toward a kind, wicked or downtrodden personality, each opening its own replies and jokes. It is party management as comedy, with you as the overworked backbone.

nearest.name: Gems are Mine, Slashes are Yours: Blood & Blessing

calibration.title: Rubble Belt Purge
calibration.short_description: A free roguelike spin on the classic rock-blasting arcade shooter. Outfit your ship with wild weapon combos, hop between planets, and wipe a shattered moon's debris out of the solar system.
calibration.description: It is the 25th century, and humanity's rocket technology has never been better, right up until a distant moon detonates and showers our solar system with tumbling rock. You are a ship captain sent to clean up the mess, traveling world to world and blasting every boulder in sight. This free arcade shooter keeps the timeless formula of rotating, thrusting and firing at rocks that shatter into smaller pieces, then layers roguelike structure on top. Each planet's sectors are generated from a seed, so routes and layouts change between attempts. Between fights, visit the store to buy weapons, special abilities and utility modules; together they offer more than a million possible builds. Fire heat-seeking missiles that hunt the largest targets, hire drones to scoop up cash for you, freeze the clock, or call in a nuclear strike. Pump enough into engine speed and your ship becomes a battering ram that punches straight through debris. Expect variety in the opposition too, from golden rocks that fracture into extra fragments to flying saucers that copy your own arsenal and turn it against you. A level editor lets you craft custom challenges.

calibration.title: Little Grid Metropolis
calibration.short_description: Grow a tiny village into a sprawling pixel-art metropolis. Zone districts, lay out roads and rail, keep services running, and expand across an entire region, with saves that carry over to the phone editions.
calibration.description: Start with a handful of streets on empty land and watch it swell into a bustling urban center, then do it again in neighboring towns across a wide region. This retro-styled management sim hands you the full toolkit of a city planner. Designate areas for homes, shops and factories, run power lines and water pipes, and keep an eye on congestion as residents demand more from you with every milestone. Transport is a game of its own: plan bus routes, lay rail lines, build airports and connect everything with highways, choosing which vehicles serve each line to keep people moving efficiently. Trouble never stays away for long. Blazes, rising crime, smog, epidemics and natural catastrophes all test your emergency services. Fund schools, hospitals and other public facilities to lift quality of life and sustain growth over decades. Add famous monuments and grand wonders to your skyline, or download fan-made plugins that introduce fresh buildings, systems and customization. The PC release is the complete package, with every extra included and no advertisements or microtransactions, and it plays nicely with the phone and tablet editions.

calibration.title: Starfish Slacker: Reef Rampage
calibration.short_description: Become a lovably dim pink starfish and turn a sleepy undersea town into your personal playground of physics-driven chaos, wacky stunts and pointless, glorious goofing off.
calibration.description: Deep beneath the waves sits a cheerful little town full of quirky neighbors, a burger joint, an amusement park and a junkyard, and for once its laziest resident is the star. You play a happily clueless starfish free to roam the whole open world and cause as much ruckus as he likes. Nearly every object can be grabbed, shoved, tossed or used. Point a blower at the reef, splash paint across buildings, or haul something somewhere it absolutely does not belong and watch the physics take over. Leap from great heights clutching only an umbrella, dig through heaps of trash for hidden loot, or smash everything in a room built for venting anger. Pulling off ridiculous stunts and finding collectibles earns new costumes for his wardrobe. Friends around town, including a sponge neighbor, a squirrel scientist, a greedy restaurant owner and a tiny scheming rival, hand out silly challenges. Or ignore all of it and try to sit still and do nothing longer than seems humanly possible. There are no wrong ways to play, only funny ones.

calibration.title: Shared Vessel
calibration.short_description: You come to in a sealed laboratory and realize another mind is sharing your body. Explore, gather clues and fight for control of yourself in a short pixel-art horror adventure with several endings.
calibration.description: You open your eyes in a research lab you do not recognize, the subject of a cold and deranged scientist's project. Worse, you are not alone in your own head: another consciousness has taken up residence inside you, and it wants your body for itself. The tragedy that led here is buried somewhere in these rooms. Progress is driven by four command buttons along the top of the screen, though not every command can be used at every moment, and figuring out when and how to act is part of the puzzle. Search rooms, inspect objects and collect items, then decide for yourself where each one should be applied. At key points you will clash with the intruder in a struggle over who controls your mind, and winning those contests is the only way to reclaim yourself. Documents and evidence scattered across the facility slowly reveal who this other person is, why you are trapped, and what the experiment was meant to achieve. Expect a run of roughly five hours, several possible conclusions, a hint menu for each ending, and unflinching scenes of death and bloodshed.

calibration.title: Last Light Detachment
calibration.short_description: Lead a hand-picked strike team through a grim, single-player campaign of turn-based tactical missions as a galaxy-spanning war nears its bloody end and a darker menace begins to rise.
calibration.description: In the final, exhausted months of a war that has engulfed the galaxy, a former officer is pulled back into service to head a covert unit of specialists. Their assignment brings them face to face with a new danger that could swallow every star system if no one stops it. You guide this squad through a cinematic original story told across tense tactical operations, investigations and rescue missions. On the battlefield, combat plays out in turns on shifting terrain where positioning, cover and timing decide who walks away. Between deployments, manage your headquarters, plan the next move and live with the consequences of your choices, which shape each campaign differently. Build your roster from a mix of roles, from smugglers and loyal repair droids to a mystic warrior wielding a glowing blade, and draw on a deep pool of tactical abilities to outthink your enemies. Operatives grow as they fight together, unlocking teamwork combos that can turn a losing engagement around. Design your commander's specialty and look, then recruit and outfit original characters with custom gear, skills and appearance.

calibration.title: Dead Man's Beat
calibration.short_description: Murdered and then revived by a parasitic organism, a hard-boiled cop joins a covert unit to stop the mob responsible for his death from turning his unnatural immortality into a weapon. Free, fast and bloody.
calibration.description: Straight out of a yellowed crime tabloid comes a free, compact action game that blends horror with a dark sense of humor. You play a police investigator who was gunned down by mobsters, only to be dragged back to life by a parasite now living inside him. A shadowy government unit puts him to work, and the mission is personal: track down the outfit that murdered him before they figure out how to harness the same deathless power for their own ends. Each stage is a mostly linear run of tight hallways packed with hoodlums and hired muscle. Gun them down, keep your momentum, and find the fastest line through every room, shaving seconds off each attempt as you learn the layout. Death is not the end here; it is part of the rhythm, and you will drop and get back up constantly. Inspired by frantic one-hit action games and speed-focused shooters, it pairs that twitchy pace with hand-drawn art in the style of vintage pulp detective comics, all ink-heavy shadows and lurid panels.

calibration.title: Second Chance Paws: Prologue
calibration.short_description: Run a rescue shelter for dogs and cats: feed, clean, cuddle and even dress up your residents, hire helpers, and match each animal with the right new owner. Bring friends along in online co-op.
calibration.description: This prologue offers a first taste of a larger animal rescue simulation, and a new set of furry residents are waiting for someone to look after them. Day to day, you keep kennels spotless, fill bowls with food and fresh water, and give every dog and cat the attention it craves through play, petting and the occasional outfit. Healthy, happy animals are easier to place, but caring for everyone alone quickly becomes overwhelming. Bring on staff to share the workload, assigning tasks and keeping your team motivated, because handling people takes its own kind of skill. You do not have to run things solo either: invite friends to join your shelter online, divide up chores, chat with emotes, and enjoy the pretty surroundings together. The heart of the experience is adoption. Visitors stop by to meet the animals in person, and your job is to read both sides carefully, pairing each pet with a household that truly suits it, and the reverse. Patience and good judgment lead to happy endings for animals and families alike.

nearest.name: Pet Shelter Simulator: The Ultimate Animal Shop Experience

calibration.title: Feint & Counter
calibration.short_description: An arcade brawler reimagined as a head-to-head card game: master a fighter's deck, chain combos and outguess your rival's next move. Designed by a veteran fighting game competitor and proven over years of tournament play.
calibration.description: Everything that makes a one-on-one fighting game thrilling, the guesswork, the combos, the mind games, gets translated into cards here. Each player chooses a fighter with a unique deck, and every exchange begins with both sides secretly selecting a move and revealing at once. Knowing your character's strengths and predicting what your rival will try next is how matches are won, and a successful hit lets you chain additional cards into damaging combos. The design comes from a longtime tournament competitor who led the rebalance of a celebrated arcade fighter, and it has supported a competitive scene for many years, even earning a game of the year nod from a prominent tabletop reviewer. Ten fighters are included, with ten more sold as add-ons. Learn the basics in the tutorial, practice against computer opponents up to a genuinely tough expert level, or test your stamina in a survival gauntlet. Online matches support cross-play with mobile players, ranked ladders take you from novice to master, and you can save your own replays or watch anyone else's, including the best on the leaderboards.

calibration.title: Gaslight Hunt: The Blighted Moon
calibration.short_description: A clockwork-fantasy roguelite deckbuilder set in a Victorian city: pick one of four agents with their own cards and talents and hunt the source of a blight twisting wildlife into monsters. Earn relics and magical tarot cards as you go.
calibration.description: In a city of brass, steam and smoke, something has gone badly wrong with the creatures of the wilds. A creeping sickness is twisting animals into savage monstrosities, and a group of agents is dispatched to learn where it began and how to stop it. Set before the events of an earlier adventure in the same universe, this narrative roguelite spans four chapters of eerie encounters, missions, new regions and fearsome bosses. Choose your investigator: a towering bruiser who flattens anything in the way, a disciplined veteran with a mastery of firearms, an alchemist armed with tonics, toxins and bombs, or a fourth agent with talents of their own. Each comes with a distinct card pool, and you shape your deck from hundreds of options, upgrading cards to make them hit harder. Fights play out in turns through shadowy forests and crooked alleys, where reading an enemy's habits is the key to survival. Whether a mission ends in triumph or a hasty retreat, you bring home coin, cards, gear, relics and scrap to strengthen your agents and your airship for the next run.

nearest.name: Hunter's Moon: A Sovereign Syndicate Adventure

calibration.title: Feral Free-for-All
calibration.short_description: Pit dinosaurs, wild animals and people against each other in a gory physics sandbox. Strap guns and bombs onto them, build teams, and watch the ragdoll carnage unfold.
calibration.description: This battle simulator lets you assemble absurd armies of prehistoric reptiles, modern wildlife and humans, drop them onto a field, and watch what happens. Everything runs on full physics, so creatures shove, topple and slam into one another in unpredictable ways, and a well-placed bite or blast can tear off a limb. Each species fights with its own moves and attack habits, so matchups really matter. Want to see a herd of explosive zebras charge a laser-armed tyrannosaur, or a swarm of gulls take on gun-toting lions? Set it up. You can bolt weapons onto any beast, from automatic rifles to flamethrowers to strapped-on bombs. Beyond free play, a puzzle-like challenge mode offers sixty scenarios where you must pick the right team to meet a goal, such as knocking down stacks of crates or surviving a confrontation with a fearsome penguin monarch. There is even a sports mode where animals compete in brutal football matches, so you can finally learn whether long-necked sauropods outplay polar bears on the pitch. The game is still in early development, with more to come.

calibration.title: Open Mic Odyssey
calibration.short_description: A free retro point-and-click comedy about a broke rookie stand-up chasing the title of funniest person alive. Three gigs, one notebook full of half-baked jokes, and a lot of awkward silence to overcome.
calibration.description: Stand-up comedy is a strange, enchanted world, and this short, free adventure drops you right into it. You play an eager beginner who has only ever performed at open mic nights, dreaming of becoming the funniest comic on the planet. Your starting kit is pitiful: empty pockets and a notebook for scribbling down material. Across three shows, you explore locations, talk with oddball characters, gather items and combine them to solve puzzles, all while hunting for the inspiration that might turn into a killer bit. The look harks back to the chunky pixel art of classic eighties adventures, while the tone and puzzle design lean toward the playful, character-driven style of the best nineties graphic adventures. A fully voiced cast drawn from real working comedians brings the backstage weirdos, hecklers and fellow performers to life. Every venue brings new obstacles between you and the microphone, and every conversation could hand you a punchline or a dead end. Point, click, scribble, and try to survive the spotlight.

nearest.name: Detective Boiled-Hard / Case File - Death of the Space Dino Hunter
There Is No Game: Wrong Dimension

calibration.title: Circuit Tiles: Endless Logic
calibration.short_description: A calm, minimalist puzzle game where you slide jigsaw-like tiles into place to complete working digital logic circuits, set to a gentle, soothing soundtrack.
calibration.description: Part jigsaw, part electronics lesson, this quiet puzzle game asks you to arrange scattered tiles so they join into functioning digital circuits. Every board presents a goal and a set of pieces, each printed with wires and gates such as AND, OR and NOT. Drag them around the board and fit them together until signals flow correctly from inputs to outputs. Early stages ease you in with simple connections, while later ones demand a real grasp of how gates combine and behave. With over a hundred and thirty boards of rising difficulty, and pieces shuffled into new arrangements each time, no two sessions feel quite the same. The pace is entirely yours. A soft, relaxing score plays in the background while you work through clean, brightly tinted scenes with plenty of space to think. Whether you already understand boolean logic or are picking it up as you go, the steady rhythm of placing a tile and watching a circuit come to life makes it an easy game to unwind with.

calibration.title: Static Front: Grid Duelists
calibration.short_description: Build a deck of attacks and fight in real time on a split tile grid. Push back a creeping corruption in the story campaign, or test your build against others online with rollback netcode.
calibration.description: A world teeters on the edge of all-out war, a place of spinning cities, violet frozen wastelands and strange realms made of pure data, and two teenagers end up caught at the center of the conflict. Battles happen on a grid divided between you and your foe. You dash between tiles to dodge incoming fire while drawing from a deck of attack chips you assembled yourself, unleashing them in fast real-time exchanges. Play through a lengthy campaign against a spreading static corruption, collecting new cards, shaping your hero and digging up secrets the world would rather keep buried, as enemies grow tougher. Over twenty playable characters and thousands of custom moves give you room to craft a style all your own. When you think your build is ready, challenge friends locally or face rivals online, where rollback networking keeps matches responsive. A friendly built-in creator lets you design fresh maps, fighters and loadouts with no programming knowledge required, then share your mods with the community.

calibration.title: Burned Asset
calibration.short_description: Branded a traitor by the intelligence agency she once served, a fugitive operative must slip through a neon-lit surveillance state, hiding in plain sight while she works to prove her innocence.
calibration.description: She spent years working for the agency. Now she is its most wanted target, accused of betraying her country on evidence someone planted. In this first-person stealth game you guide the disgraced operative as she flees, lies low and digs for the truth that could exonerate her. Stick to dark corners, keep your footsteps quiet and stay clear of every guard's line of sight. When cornered, blind pursuers with gadgets that disrupt their vision, and boost your abilities with illicit drugs bought from underground dealers. The setting is a cold, modern police state rendered in raw concrete slabs and glowing neon signage, where cameras watch every street. Across eight missions on two continents you will encounter a varied cast, from old contacts willing to risk everything for you to new acquaintances whose loyalties are far less certain. With the whole world hunting you, deciding whom to trust matters. Driving it all is an eighteen-track score of synth-soaked electronic rock written for the game.

calibration.title: Lightbearer's Quiet Journey
calibration.short_description: A gentle, unhurried puzzle adventure through haunting, carefully designed architecture. Guide a small glowing wanderer, solve clever mechanical riddles, and restore light to a lifeless world.
calibration.description: A small being made of light wanders through vast, silent structures in this calm puzzle adventure, crafted by two brothers who trained as architects. The world has gone dark, and your aim is to gather the scattered light and return life to the empty halls. Each scene is a striking piece of architecture full of eerie stillness and soft music, built to be absorbed slowly. Click to move your little guide and interact with the surroundings, press a key to set objects down, and use the arrow keys to shift the machinery around you. Every stage introduces a fresh twist, nudging you to think in new ways rather than repeat old solutions. Across nine distinct chapters you will find two dozen levels holding more than thirty puzzles, adding up to somewhere between ninety minutes and three hours of play. First released on phones to strong reviews, the game has been rebuilt and polished for this edition. Settle in, take your time, and let the atmosphere carry you.

nearest.name: Sweet Home: Look and Find 4 Collector's Edition

calibration.title: Gobble Blob Through Time
calibration.short_description: Play a speck of gray goo that devours whatever is smaller than it, growing with every bite. Eat your way from crumbs and mice to dinosaurs, temples and whole planets across six eras of history.
calibration.description: It starts as a speck of hungry gray goo with one simple rule: whatever is smaller than you is food, and every bite makes you bigger. Things get stranger when the goo gobbles up a time machine and gets flung into the past. From there you munch your way through six eras, beginning in the present day and moving on to the age of dinosaurs, the land of the pharaohs, the Roman Empire, samurai-era Japan and a far-off future. Each period comes stocked with its own menu of edibles, hundreds in total, from rodents and house cats to tyrannosaurs, mummies, arena fighters and alien spacecraft. Some stages stretch across absurd differences in scale, so a single level can take you from a single-celled organism all the way up to something as large as a galaxy. The full campaign can be shared with a second player in local cooperative play. Around fifty main stages are followed by a similar number of bonus levels that remix old areas or add brand-new ones for an extra challenge, and both gamepads and mouse with keyboard are supported.

calibration.title: Steel Column: Eastern Front
calibration.short_description: A tank warfare sim set on the Second World War's eastern front. Command a Soviet armored vehicle through a series of combat missions across two large battlefields, backed by two computer-controlled escort tanks.
calibration.description: Climb into a Soviet tank during the Second World War and fight your way through a chain of combat objectives, one after another, across two sprawling battlefields. The campaign is told entirely from the Soviet side. You steer with the keyboard and aim with the mouse, scrolling the wheel to pull the camera closer to or farther from your vehicle. You never ride alone: two allied tanks controlled by the computer roll alongside you, adding firepower and drawing enemy attention. If your own tank is knocked out, the mission carries on, and you simply take command of one of your surviving escorts. Choosing the right machine matters. Medium tanks are nimble and quick but lightly armored, and their guns pack less punch. Heavy tanks fire devastating rounds and can take a beating, yet they lumber across the field and turn slowly. Balance speed against protection, pick your angles, and push the enemy back. Before your first battle, it is worth opening the settings menu to review the control layout so you are ready when the shooting starts.

calibration.title: Rampart Deck Heroes
calibration.short_description: Hold the line against a monster invasion in a side-scrolling defense game powered by your deck. Collect skill cards, recruit allies, level up your hero and fight through stages toward a final boss.
calibration.description: Monsters are pouring into a peaceful fantasy realm, and a lone hero stands between them and everything that matters. This 2D game merges side-scrolling defense battles with deck construction. As waves of creatures advance toward your position, you draw from a hand of cards, each one triggering a different skill, and choosing which to play and when decides whether the line holds. Every foe you cut down earns experience, which lets you level up and strengthen your hero's abilities as the campaign goes on. Along the way you gather new cards and recruit companions, refining your deck into a combination that suits your approach. Enemy types vary widely, each with its own tricks, so a build that crushes one stage might struggle in the next. Push through increasingly dangerous levels, adapt as the threats grow, and finally confront the boss leading the invasion. Clever planning matters, but so does a little luck of the draw. Bright, cheerful art keeps the tone light even when the screen is swarming with enemies.
